target_customer: Ordinary people who wanted a biography page and a record of who they are connected to, without Wikipedia's notability bar
problem: Wikipedia only covers notable people, so most people could not have a biography page. Biographicon was a wiki for biographies of famous and non famous people showing how they connect.
business_model: Free consumer wiki, monetization not stated

founders.name: Ethan Herdrick
founders.background_notes: YC page bio reads software engineer

founders.name: Daniel Terhorst
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the Wikipedia article; YC page listing reported by search

exit.reason: Founders cited insufficient user interest in the site; a brief revival attempt failed

technical_complexity.rationale: A wiki with biographies and relationship links, standard web engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Wiki content was easy to replicate, and the only lock in would have come from user pages and connections that never reached scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wikipedia did not respond; its notability bar was the gap Biographicon targeted. The site closed in August 2008.

market_need_then: Press at launch showed curiosity: The Wired Campus, The Independent and Ars Technica covered the idea, while TechCrunch's Arrington doubted it would gain traction. Founders later cited insufficient user interest.

branding.domain_note: biographicon.com now returns a 403 error in this session

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline was all the people of the world

branding.brand_signature: Wikipedia for non-notables, the nickname given by The Wired Campus
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the concept from The Wired Campus, The Independent and Ars Technica, per the Wikipedia article. No sign of an active community.

brand_strength.rationale: The concept earned a memorable press nickname and a Wikipedia article, but the name is long and the site lasted about five months.

outcome_analysis: Biographicon joined YC in Summer 2007, launched on 1 March 2008 and closed on 21 August 2008, according to its Wikipedia article. The founders said the site had insufficient user interest. A wiki of everyone has a cold start problem because the pages are only worth visiting once many people have filled them in. The launch press was curious but the site never reached that point, and a revival attempt shortly after the closure failed.
notes: Seed round date is 2007 only and the amount is not stated; it rests on the Wikipedia article saying a small amount of YC seed money was received. Competitor list is empty because no source dated near the batch was found; Wikipedia is the obvious reference but was named only in a later page. The YC listing says one founder, and Wikipedia names two. Education and prior employers were not found. Site returned 403 so no site content was read. Wikipedia says the site ran March to August 2008 while YC dates the company to 2007, so founding in 2007 and public launch in 2008 is inferred.
